newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela, Colombia to investigate border problems.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela, Colombia to investigate border problems.

text.p: Venezuela and Colombia began an investigation on Tuesday into a spate of border incidents such as the kidnapping of a U.S. oil engineer and his pilot, the Venezuelan and Colombian foreign ministries said.
"The desire is to perfect already existing mechanisms to verify incidents that happen (on the border)," the ministries said in a statement announcing the creation of a commission.

Jerel Schaffer, an employee of the Houston, Texas-based Production Operators Inc., was snatched on Feb. 14 with his Venezuelan pilot Elias Eduardo Barando at the start of a fishing trip in the southestern border state of Apure, more than 530 miles (850 km) southwest of Caracas.
Barando was freed on Friday, Defence Ministry officials said, but Schaffer had not been heard from. He was the first U.S. citizen to be kidnapped in Venezuela since 1993.
On Friday the U.S. Embassy warned U.S. citizens "to exercise a high level of caution when travelling in areas along the Venezuelan-Colombian border."

Venezuelan authorities have said the pair were most likely victims of frequent incursions by leftist Colombian guerrillas that resulted in several kidnappings in February. Kidnapping, smuggling and drug trafficking along Venezuela's sparsely populated 1,400 mile (2,200 km) border with Colombia have increasingly strained relations between the two countries.
